# About this site {#sec-about-site .unnumbered}

This site holds a book on affine Toda field theory and three courses of lecture notes that accompany it.

Affine Toda field theories are two-dimensional quantum field theories, one for each affine Kac–Moody algebra. They are integrable, so many of their properties can be computed exactly. They have particles and bound states, solitons and breathers, strong–weak duality and quantum-group symmetry. They admit integrable boundaries and defects, and at imaginary coupling they are non-unitary.

## The book {#sec-about-book .unnumbered}

*Affine Toda field theory: A unified review, with new results* gathers results from five decades of papers. It presents them in a logical order, in one notation and with one set of conventions. Most statements come with a proof, and many formulas with a script that checks them. The book is a reference, not a course. Its nine parts run from the physical and algebraic background, through the classical theory and the quantum theory at real and at imaginary coupling, to the half-line, defects and the foundations of the non-unitary theory.

- The [preface](preface.qmd) describes the nine parts, and the [introduction](01-introduction.qmd) sets out six reading paths through them.
- Two appendices list the book's [original results](appendices/E-original-results.qmd) and its [corrections to published papers](appendices/D-corrections.qmd).
- The whole book is also available as a [PDF](https://gustavdelius.github.io/affine_toda/affine-toda.pdf).

## A course on the half-line {#sec-about-half-line .unnumbered}

The book states results but does not teach them step by step. Lecture notes do that for single parts, and link into the book for its statements and proofs.

- [*Lectures on affine Toda field theory on the half-line*](https://gustavdelius.github.io/affine_toda/lectures/half-line/) ([PDF](https://gustavdelius.github.io/affine_toda/lectures/half-line/half-line.pdf)), drafted by Gemini, accompanies Part VII, on integrable boundaries. It is organized around five big ideas and uses $a_1^{(1)}$ (sine-Gordon and sinh-Gordon) and $a_2^{(1)}$ as worked laboratories. Its six lectures cover both the classical and the quantum theory: the $90^\circ$ Euclidean rotation to a boundary state and boundary crossing-unitarity, Sklyanin's double-row monodromy matrix and why higher-rank boundary couplings freeze to $C_j\in\{0,\pm1\}$, mirror solitons and non-constant vacua, coideal subalgebras and the Ghoshal–Zamolodchikov reflection matrix, $a_2^{(1)}$ intertwiners and generalized $q$-Onsager algebras, and the route from solitons through breathers to real-coupling particle reflection amplitudes and weak–strong boundary duality. Each lecture has set-piece blackboard calculations, guided rediscovery exercises and a check script in `code/lectures/`.

## Two courses on integrable defects {#sec-about-lectures .unnumbered}

Two further courses accompany Part VIII, on integrable defects. A defect is a line in spacetime that particles and solitons cross without being reflected. They were drafted by different AI models, and they teach the subject in different ways.

- [*Integrable defects, from Bäcklund to Baxter*](https://gustavdelius.github.io/affine_toda/lectures/defects/) ([PDF](https://gustavdelius.github.io/affine_toda/lectures/defects/defects.pdf)), drafted by Claude, tells the story of the ideas. Each lecture asks one question and answers it. All nine lectures are written. Lectures 1–6 cover the classical theory, and Lectures 7–9 cover quantum transmission, Q-operators and boundary fusion.
- [*Lectures on integrable defects in affine Toda field theory*](https://gustavdelius.github.io/affine_toda/lectures/defects-gemini/) ([PDF](https://gustavdelius.github.io/affine_toda/lectures/defects-gemini/defects-gemini.pdf)), drafted by Gemini, is organized around six big ideas. Its six lectures are complete and cover both the classical and the quantum theory.

### How they differ {#sec-about-differences .unnumbered}

| | *Integrable defects, from Bäcklund to Baxter* | *Lectures on integrable defects* |
|---|---|---|
| Written so far | All 9 lectures | All 6 lectures |
| Scope | The classical theory in Lectures 1–6: point defects, Bäcklund transformations, defect conditions, solitons, Lax matrices and r-matrices. The quantum theory in Lectures 7–9: transmission matrices, Q-operators and boundary fusion | The classical theory in Lectures 1–3. The quantum theory in Lectures 4–6: Borel subalgebras, $q$-oscillators and Baxter's $Q$-operators, crossing and the sign of $q$, quantum tunnelling in $a_2^{(1)}$, defects meeting boundaries, breathers |
| Pace | Slow. The classical theory takes six lectures. It starts from a $\delta$-function defect in a free field and from the surface geometry behind Bäcklund's construction | Fast. The classical theory takes three lectures, with sine-Gordon theory and $a_2^{(1)}$ as the main examples |
| Style | One question per lecture, *Predict* boxes that ask you to guess a result before you calculate it, short declarative sentences, figures | Six big ideas, set-piece "blackboard calculations" with every step written out, an enthusiastic voice, figures |
| Exercises | 84, of three kinds: redo, rediscover and explore | 14 guided problems |
| Checks | Every calculation shown in detail is checked by a script in `code/lectures/`, written from the lectures' own definitions | Figure scripts in `code/lectures/` check the plotted formulas and exercises; the main text also cites the book's scripts |

### Which to read {#sec-about-which .unnumbered}

Read *Integrable defects, from Bäcklund to Baxter* if you want to see where each idea comes from and to do every calculation yourself, and if the classical theory is enough for now. Read the other course if you want the whole arc in six lectures, from the no-go theorem for reflection and transmission to the quantum transmission matrices, or if you are heading for the quantum theory. The first halves of the two courses cover the same ground, so they can be read side by side. Where they do the same calculation in different ways, comparing them is instructive.

## How the site was made {#sec-about-made .unnumbered}

The book and *Integrable defects, from Bäcklund to Baxter* were drafted by Claude, an AI model made by Anthropic, and *Lectures on affine Toda field theory on the half-line* and *Lectures on integrable defects in affine Toda field theory* by Gemini, an AI model made by Google. They worked from outlines, source papers and briefs assembled by the editor, Gustav Delius. Further instances of Claude, Codex and Gemini have checked the book as referees. Validation is by AI agents only; human readers contribute by giving feedback. Main results carry a status label, such as **[Theorem]**, **[Established]**, **[Numerical]** or **[Conjecture]**, that says how they were established, and the [preface](preface.qmd) describes how the book was written. Where a result matters to you, check the proof, and run the scripts.

The Quarto sources, the check scripts and the record of the checks are on [GitHub](https://github.com/gustavdelius/affine_toda). If you find an error or something unclear, please [open an issue](https://github.com/gustavdelius/affine_toda/issues) there.

:::
